tool-format.description: when the light tier's escalate tool is called, it must carry a real reason string and a suggested_tier in escalate.py's own enum (heavy_local, claude).

no-tool.description: a trivial, directly-answerable prompt must not invoke any tool at all.

escalation-accuracy.description: fraction of a small varied prompt set (some that clearly need escalation, some that clearly don't) where the model's escalate/don't-escalate decision matched expectation. min_pass_rate is 1.0 at qubi_bench.py's current n=2 sample size deliberately -- 0.8 of 2 rounds down to '1 wrong still passes,' which would defeat the gate.

append-vs-overwrite.description: an append instruction must produce a real append, not a full-file overwrite -- requires the developer extension (file tools); reports skip on tiers that don't have it (light, by design).

no-phantom-write.description: a claimed file write must actually exist on disk with the claimed content, not just be described in the response text -- requires the developer extension; reports skip on tiers that don't have it.

latency.description: worst observed TTFT across the gate suite's own turns vs this tier's <tier>_ttft_ms in ~/.config/qubi/config.json's latency_budgets -- the threshold lives there, not duplicated here.

game-qa.description: read-only: when /run/ai-workstation/state.json reports state=gaming, the light tier's reported model must be its cpu_model, not the GPU model. Reports skip when not currently gaming -- this CLI never writes that root-owned file to force the state.
